images.title: Cancel the pairs
images.purpose: Show that 5 green tokens and 3 red tokens make 3 zero pairs, leaving 2 green tokens, which is floor +2.
images.composition: Two aligned rows of tokens stacked with generous spacing, and one result label to the right of the lower row.
images.exact_structure: Top row: 5 equal round green tokens (teal #0072B2) in a line, evenly spaced. Below it, bottom row: 3 equal round red tokens (reddish purple #CC79A7) placed directly under the first 3 green tokens. Three short grey #6B7280 vertical links join each red token to the green token above it, marking 3 pairs. The last 2 green tokens have no link and are ringed in amber #E69F00. Exactly 5 green tokens, 3 red tokens, 3 links, 2 ringed.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Each red and green pair cancels; what is left tells the floor.
images.description: 5 green tokens over 3 red tokens joined in 3 pairs, with the last 2 green tokens ringed and labelled +2.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the pairs, then say what colour is left and how many.

image_decisions.why: Cancelling zero pairs is a picture idea; two aligned rows carry it.
